items.followUp: What happens to a cell during interphase and the mitotic phase?

rubric.why: Checks the definition of the cell cycle as the sequence in which a cell grows and divides.
rubric.description: Defines the cell cycle as a series of events in which a cell grows and divides.

rubric.why: Checks that both main phases are named.
rubric.description: Names interphase and the mitotic phase as the two main phases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both phases.

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the series of events through which a cell grows and divides to form two daughter cells.
Its two main phases are interphase and the mitotic phase (M phase).
During interphase, the cell grows and replicates its DNA; during the mitotic phase, the cell divides.

items.followUp: Explain how an enzyme acts on its substrate according to the lock-and-key model.

rubric.why: Checks the model’s key idea: a substrate fits a specifically shaped enzyme active site.
rubric.description: Defines the lock-and-key model as the complementary fit of a substrate into an enzyme’s active site.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the complementary fit.

rubric.why: Checks the essential labelled stages of the diagram, including product release and the enzyme remaining unchanged.
rubric.description: Shows the enzyme–substrate complex, products leaving, and the unchanged enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a recognisable sequence showing these stages.

modelAnswer: In the lock-and-key model, an enzyme’s active site has a specific shape complementary to its substrate, which fits into it like a key in a lock.
Diagram: draw and label an enzyme with a shaped active site and a matching substrate approaching it.
Show the substrate fitted into the active site and label the enzyme–substrate complex.
Show the products leaving the enzyme; the enzyme remains unchanged.

items.followUp: What is the function of the pericardial fluid?

rubric.why: Checks the defining structure of the pericardium.
rubric.description: Identifies the pericardium as a double membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its structure.

rubric.why: Checks the position of the pericardium in relation to the heart.
rubric.description: States that the pericardium surrounds the heart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating what it surrounds.

modelAnswer: The pericardium is a double membrane that surrounds the heart.
It protects the heart; fluid between the membranes reduces friction as the heart beats.

items.followUp: Name and briefly explain four biological careers related to health, food production or the environment.

rubric.why: Checks for a biological profession and a relevant description of its work.
rubric.description: Medicine: doctors use biological knowledge to diagnose, prevent or treat diseases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the profession and giving a relevant explanation.

rubric.why: Checks for a profession applying biology to crop production.
rubric.description: Agriculture: agriculturists apply biology to improve crops and food production.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the profession and giving a relevant explanation.

rubric.why: Checks for a profession applying biology to fish or aquatic resources.
rubric.description: Fisheries: fisheries professionals manage or breed fish and other aquatic resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the profession and giving a relevant explanation.

rubric.why: Checks for a profession applying biology to forest management or conservation.
rubric.description: Forestry: foresters manage and conserve forests and their resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the profession and giving a relevant explanation.

modelAnswer: Medicine: doctors use biological knowledge to diagnose, prevent and treat diseases in humans.
Agriculture: agriculturists apply biology to improve crops and increase food production.
Fisheries: fisheries professionals manage or breed fish and other aquatic resources.
Forestry: foresters manage and conserve forests and their resources.
